docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನಿದಂ ಪ್ರೋತಂ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸ ಏವ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾಖ್ಯಃ ಸ್ವಾವಯವೇ ಮಾಸೇ ಕೃತ್ಸ್ನಃ ಪರಿಸಮಾಪ್ಯತೇ ।

ಮಾಸೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣ ಏವ ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ।

ತಸ್ಯ ಮಾಸಾತ್ಮನಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರೇಕೋ ಭಾಗಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ ಅಪರೋ ಭಾಗಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಆದಿತ್ಯೋಽತ್ತಾಗ್ನಿಃ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇಽಪೀಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ತೈರ್ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ;

ಇತರೇ ತು ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತೀತ್ಯದರ್ಶನಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾತ್ಮಾನಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ ।

ಇತರೇ ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
That very Prajāpati, named the Saṃvatsara (Year), in whom all this world is strung — he is completely contained within his own limb, the Month (Māsa).

The Month is indeed Prajāpati — with exactly the characteristics as described (the Year), and of the dyadic nature (mithunātmaka — of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa).

Of that Prajāpati whose nature is the Month, one portion is the dark fortnight — which is Rayi, food, the Moon; the other portion is the bright — the bright fortnight — which is Prāṇa, the Sun, the eater, the fire.

Because these seers see all as Prāṇa — as the one who is the Self of the bright fortnight — therefore, these seers who are perceivers of Prāṇa, even when performing their sacrificial rites (iṣṭa / yāga) in the dark fortnight, perform them in the bright fortnight alone.

For by them, the dark fortnight is not seen as anything apart from Prāṇa.

The others, however, not seeing Prāṇa — they see only what is of the nature of darkness (non-perceiving, kṛṣṇa).

The others perform in the dark fortnight alone — even when performing in the bright.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
Two sentences in this Bhāṣya require explicit anvaya treatment.

Sentence 1 — Seers perform in the bright even when in the dark

As written:

ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇಽಪಿ ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನಃ [ಸಂತಃ] — ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ-ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ಅಪಿ ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ [ಅಪಿ] ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

English: These seers, being perceivers of Prāṇa — because they see Prāṇa (whose Self is the bright fortnight) as everything — therefore, even while performing the sacrifice in the dark fortnight, they perform in the bright fortnight alone.

Note: The yasmat…tasmāt (because…therefore) frame spans the entire sentence. The participial ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ (while performing) and the finite verb ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ (they perform) are both needed — one states the physical occasion (dark fortnight), the other states the ontological reality (bright fortnight). Ānandagiri flags this as the core anvaya difficulty.

Sentence 2 — Others perform in the dark even when in the bright

As written:

ಇತರೇ ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಇತರೇ [ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಃ] — ಶುಕ್ಲೇ [ಪಕ್ಷೇ] ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

English: The others — not seeing Prāṇa — even while performing in the bright fortnight, perform in the dark fortnight alone.

Note: This sentence is the exact parallel and inversion of Sentence 1 — same structure (participial + finite verb), opposite result. Ānandagiri's Ṭīkā makes the symmetry explicit: just as knowledge transforms dark into bright for the seers, ignorance transforms bright into dark for the others.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಕಾರಣತ್ವೇ ಶ್ಲೋಕೋಕ್ತಂ ಜಗದಾಶ್ರಯತ್ವಂ ಹೇತುಮಾಹ – ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನಿತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಮಾಸಾಹೋರಾತ್ರರೂಪವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಔಷಧ್ಯಾದಿಜನಕತ್ವಾಭಾವಾತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಮಾಸಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಮಾಹ – ಸ ಏವೇತಿ ।

ಯಥೋಕ್ತೇತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರರೂಪಃ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಶುಕ್ಲಕೃಷ್ಣಯೋಃ ಉಭಯೋಃ ಅಪಿ ದರ್ಶಪೂರ್ಣಮಾಸಾದಿಕರ್ಮಾನುಷ್ಠಾನದರ್ಶನಾತ್ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಅನುಪಪನ್ನಮ್ ಇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಶುಕ್ಲಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ತುತಿಪರತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಯಸ್ಮಾದಿತಿ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಃ ತೈಃ ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಾದಿಸರ್ವಜಗತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣದ್ವಾರಾ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷತ್ವೇ ಸತಿ ಕೃಷ್ಣೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಾತ್ಮಕೇ ಶುಕ್ಲ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಇತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ಯ ಸ್ತುತಿಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಏತತ್ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯರ್ಥಮೇವ ಜ್ಞಾನರಹಿತಾನ್ ನಿಂದತಿ – ಇತರೇ ತ್ವಿತಿ ।

ಯೇ ತು ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತ್ಯಜ್ಞತ್ವಾತ್ ತೇಷಾಂ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವೇನ ಅಜ್ಞಾಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಸನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷತ್ವಮಾಪದ್ಯತೇ ಅತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ಅದರ್ಶನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಕಾಶರಹಿತೇ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಇತಿ ತೇ ನಿಂದ್ಯಂತೇ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಉಕ್ತಮರ್ಥಂ ಶ್ರುತ್ಯಾ ಆರೂಢಂ ಕರೋತಿ – ಇತರ ಇತಿ ॥ ೧೨ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by saying that Śaṅkara, in order to state the reason for the world-support (jagadāśrayatva) mentioned in the śloka as proof of causality (kāraṇatva), begins with "yasmin" (in whom).

Then, to show that the Year too — without the Month, day, and night — has no capacity to produce herbs etc., and therefore the Year is of the nature of the Month etc., Śaṅkara says "sa eva" (that very one). On "yathoktam" (as described): Ānandagiri explains this means "of the form of the Year, of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair."

Ānandagiri then raises an objection: since we see the performance of darśa- pūrṇamāsa (fortnightly sacrificial rites) and other rites in both the bright and dark fortnights, the Śruti statement "therefore these seers perform in the bright" would be contradicted — it would be inconsistent (anupapanna). To resolve this, Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's passage beginning "yasmāt" is aimed at praising the knowledge that the bright fortnight is the Self of Prāṇa — not at making a purely factual claim about when rites are performed.

The anvaya is: because (yasmāt) they see Prāṇa as everything, as the Self of all, and because (yasmāt) the dark fortnight is not seen by them as anything apart from Prāṇa — therefore (tasmāt) they perform in the bright alone.

Since Prāṇa is of the nature of the bright fortnight, and since all the world including the dark fortnight is of the nature of Prāṇa — through Prāṇa, the dark fortnight too becomes bright. Therefore those performing in the dark are actually performing in the bright (light-natured) alone. This is the praise (stuti) of the knowledge that the bright fortnight is Prāṇa.

For the very purpose of this praise, Śaṅkara censures those who lack this knowledge — with the words "itare tu" (the others however). Those who do not see Prāṇa as the Self of all — because they do not know the bright fortnight as Prāṇa, their bright fortnight becomes of the nature of ignorance and takes on the quality of the dark fortnight. Therefore even while performing in the bright, they perform in the dark (lightless) alone — and thus they are censured.

Finally, Ānandagiri says Śaṅkara then establishes the stated meaning through the Śruti itself — with "itara" (the other / dark fortnight).

docs.text:

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the Year · ಮಾಸಾಹೋರಾತ್ರರೂಪ-ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ — without (apart from) the Month and day-and-night form · ಔಷಧ್ಯಾದಿ-ಜನಕತ್ವ-ಅಭಾವಾತ್ — because of the absence of the capacity to produce herbs etc. · ತಸ್ಯ — of it (the Year) · ಮಾಸಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಂ — being of the nature of the Month etc. · ಆಹ — states · ಸ ಏವ ಇತಿ — with the words "sa eva (that very one)" ।

ಯಥೋಕ್ತ ಇತಿ — on the word "yathoktam (as described)" ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರರೂಪಃ — of the form of the Year · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಃ — of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಶುಕ್ಲಕೃಷ್ಣಯೋಃ ಉಭಯೋಃ ಅಪಿ — in both the bright and dark (fortnights) · ದರ್ಶಪೂರ್ಣಮಾಸಾದಿ-ಕರ್ಮ-ಅನುಷ್ಠಾನ-ದರ್ಶನಾತ್ — because of observing the performance of darśa-pūrṇamāsa and other rites · ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the statement "therefore these seers" · ಅನುಪಪನ್ನಂ — inconsistent / contradicted · ಇತಿ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this objection · ಶುಕ್ಲಸ್ಯ — of the bright (fortnight) · ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವ-ಜ್ಞಾನ-ಸ್ತುತಿ-ಪರತಯಾ — with the intent of praising the knowledge that (the bright) is the Self of Prāṇa · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the word "yasmāt (because)" ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ — because · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa · ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ — as everything · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಏವ — as the Self of all · ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — they see · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಚ — and because · ಪ್ರಾಣ-ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ — apart from Prāṇa · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಃ — the dark fortnight · ತೈಃ — by them · ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ — is not seen · ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — therefore · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ — of Prāṇa · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ-ಆತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of the bright fortnight · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಾದಿ-ಸರ್ವಜಗತಃ — of all the world including the dark fortnight · ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of Prāṇa · ಪ್ರಾಣದ್ವಾರಾ — through Prāṇa · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the dark fortnight · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷತ್ವೇ ಸತಿ — when it has the nature of the bright fortnight · ಕೃಷ್ಣೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — even while performing in the dark · ಪ್ರಕಾಶಾತ್ಮಕೇ — in what is of the nature of light · ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಏವ — in the bright alone · ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ — they perform · ಇತಿ — thus · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ಯ — of the knowledge that the bright fortnight is Prāṇa · ಸ್ತುತಿಃ — praise · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಏತತ್ — this (praise) · ಸ್ತುತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಏವ — for the very purpose of this praise · ಜ್ಞಾನರಹಿತಾನ್ — those devoid of knowledge · ನಿಂದತಿ — censures · ಇತರೇ ತು ಇತಿ — with the words "itare tu (the others however)" ।

ಯೇ ತು — those who however · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa as the Self of all · ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — do not see · ಅಜ್ಞತ್ವಾತ್ — because of ignorance · ತೇಷಾಂ — for them · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ — the bright fortnight · ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವೇನ ಅಜ್ಞಾಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ — because it is not known as Prāṇa · ಅಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಸನ್ — being of the nature of ignorance · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷತ್ವಂ ಆಪದ್ಯತೇ — takes on the nature of the dark fortnight · ಅತಃ — therefore · ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — even while performing in the bright · ಅದರ್ಶನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of non-seeing / darkness · ಪ್ರಕಾಶರಹಿತೇ — in what is devoid of light · ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಏವ — in the dark alone · ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ — they perform · ಇತಿ — thus · ತೇ ನಿಂದ್ಯಂತೇ — they are censured · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಉಕ್ತಂ ಅರ್ಥಂ — the stated meaning · ಶ್ರುತ್ಯಾ — through the Śruti · ಆರೂಢಂ ಕರೋತಿ — establishes / confirms with authority · ಇತರ ಇತಿ — with the word "itara (the other / dark fortnight)" ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Applies the Rayi-Prāṇa analysis to the Month — dark fortnight is Rayi, bright is Prāṇa; seers perform in the bright, the others in the dark ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Shows the Month as Prajāpati containing the Year; unpacks dark/bright as Moon/Sun, food/fire; explains that seers who see Prāṇa as all perform in the bright even when physically in the dark — and vice versa for the ignorant ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Resolves the apparent contradiction (anupapanna) that rites are observed in both fortnights; establishes the passage as a stuti (praise) of Prāṇa-knowledge and a nindā (censure) of ignorance; provides the full anvaya for the yasmāt…tasmāt sentence

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The Month is Prajāpati — it contains the Year completely within itself as its own limb (avayava). The Year is non-different from the Month in the same way cause and effect are non-different.
  2. Dark fortnight = Rayi = Moon = food; Bright fortnight = Prāṇa = Sun = fire. The Rayi-Prāṇa dyad operates at every level — Year, Month, fortnight.
  3. The key teaching is epistemological, not ritual: those who see Prāṇa as the Self of all transform even the dark into the bright by their knowledge. Those who do not see Prāṇa transform even the bright into the dark by their ignorance.
  4. Ānandagiri's key contribution is identifying the passage as stuti-nindā (praise and censure) — a standard Vedic rhetorical form — rather than a factual description of when rites are performed. This resolves the apparent contradiction that rites are in fact performed in both fortnights.
  5. The anvaya of yasmāt…tasmāt is the logical spine: knowledge of Prāṇa's identity with the bright fortnight means the dark fortnight is never seen as other than Prāṇa — hence performance anywhere is performance in the bright.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text: ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಹರೇವ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ರಾತ್ರಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ವಾ ಏತೇ ಪ್ರಸ್ಕಂದಂತಿ ಯೇ ದಿವಾ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದ್ಯದ್ರಾತ್ರೌ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ॥ ೧೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Day-and-Night (ahorātra) is indeed Prajāpati. Of it, the day (ahas) alone is Prāṇa and the night (rātri) alone is Rayi. Those who unite with a woman by day indeed waste / lose their Prāṇa. That which is uniting with a woman by night is brahmacarya (celibacy / proper conduct) alone.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಸೋಽಪಿ ಮಾಸಾತ್ಮಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸ್ವಾವಯವೇ ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೇ ಪರಿಸಮಾಪ್ಯತೇ ।

ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ।

ತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಅಹರೇವ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ರಾತ್ರಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವದೇವ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಮ್ ಅಹರಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೈ ಏತೇ ಪ್ರಸ್ಕಂದಂತಿ ನಿರ್ಗಮಯಂತಿ ಶೋಷಯಂತಿ ವಾ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮನೋ ವಿಚ್ಛಿದ್ಯಾಪನಯಂತಿ ।

ಕೇ ? ಯೇ ದಿವಾ ಅಹನಿ ರತ್ಯಾ ರತಿಕಾರಣಭೂತಯಾ ಸಹ ಸ್ತ್ರಿಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ಮೈಥುನಮಾಚರಂತಿ ಮೂಢಾಃ ।

ಯತ ಏವಂ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತನ್ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ।

ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ರತ್ಯಾ ಋತೌ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದಿತಿ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಯಮಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕೋ ವಿಧಿಃ ।

ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ತೂಚ್ಯತೇ ಸೋಽಹೋರಾತ್ರಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿರ್ವ್ರೀಹಿಯವಾದ್ಯನ್ನಾತ್ಮನಾ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
That Prajāpati whose nature is the Month is also completely contained within his own limb, the Day-and-Night (ahorātra).

The Day-and-Night is indeed Prajāpati — as has been stated before (with the same characteristics).

Of it too, the day alone is Prāṇa — the eater, the fire — and the night alone is Rayi — exactly as before.

Those who are foolish — they indeed lose / waste / drain away the Prāṇa whose nature is the day; they cause it to flow out, to dry up, or they cut it away and remove it from themselves.

Who are they? Those fools who by day unite with a woman — whose purpose is enjoyment — and engage in intercourse.

Since this is so, therefore this must not be done — this prohibition is incidental (prāsaṅgika — arising from the context, not the primary topic).

That which is uniting with a woman by night in the proper season (ṛtu) is brahmacarya alone — because it is praiseworthy; therefore the injunction that approaching one's wife by night in the proper season is to be done — this too is an incidental injunction (prāsaṅgika vidhi).

The main topic, however, is now stated: that Prajāpati who is of the nature of the Day-and-Night is established as food — in the form of rice, barley, and the like.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
One sentence in this Bhāṣya requires explicit anvaya treatment.

Sentence — The incidental prohibition and the incidental injunction

As written:

ಯತ ಏವಂ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತನ್ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ।

ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ರತ್ಯಾ ಋತೌ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದಿತಿ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಯಮಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕೋ ವಿಧಿಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ದಿವಾ ಮೈಥುನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಕ್ಷಯಕರಮ್] ಇತಿ ಯತಃ ಏವಂ [ಉಕ್ತಂ] — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತತ್ ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ [ಇತ್ಯಾಯಂ] ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ [ಭವತಿ] ।

[ಅಪರಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ] — ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಋತೌ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ [ತತ್] ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಂ ಏವ [ಭವತಿ] ।

[ತಸ್ಯ] ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ [ಋತೌ] ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ — ಇತಿ ಅಯಂ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ವಿಧಿಃ [ಭವತಿ] ।

English: Because intercourse by day causes loss of Prāṇa — therefore this must not be done: this prohibition is incidental (to the main topic). And conversely — that which is uniting with a woman by night in the proper season is brahmacarya alone; because of its being praiseworthy, the injunction that approaching one's wife by night in the proper season is to be done — this too is an incidental injunction.

Note: Śaṅkara uses the technical term ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕ (prāsaṅgika — incidental / arising from context) twice — once for the prohibition (pratiṣedha) and once for the positive injunction (vidhi). This signals that neither daytime abstinence nor nighttime union is the primary subject of the verse — the primary subject (ಪ್ರಕೃತ) is Prajāpati as food. Ānandagiri confirms this explicitly in the Ṭīkā.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ರಯಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ಇತಿ ।

ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅಹ್ನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಉಕ್ತಿ-ಪ್ರಸಂಗಾತ್ ಅಹ್ನಿ ಮೈಥುನಂ ನಿಷೇಧತಿ – ಪ್ರಾಣಮಿತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಕೃತಮಿತಿ ।

ಕುತೋ ಹ ವಾ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಪೂರ್ವೋಕ್ತಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏತತ್ ಉಪಯೋಗಿತಯಾ ಉಕ್ತಂ ನ ತು ಸಾಕ್ಷಾತ್ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ ॥ ೧೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
On "rāyiḥ pūrvavat" (Rayi as before): Ānandagiri explains this means Rayi is food and the Moon — i.e., the same identification as established in the earlier analysis of the Year and Month.

On the prohibition of daytime intercourse: Ānandagiri explains that by occasion of (ＵKti-prasaṅga — the incidental context of) stating the day's Prāṇa-nature, Śaṅkara prohibits intercourse by day — with the words "prāṇam" (they lose Prāṇa). This is a prāsaṅgika (incidental) prohibition arising from the context, not the primary teaching.

On "prakṛtam" (the main topic): Ānandagiri clarifies that the primary subject (prakṛta) is what was originally asked — "from where indeed are these creatures born?" — i.e., the question put to the sage at the beginning of the first Praśna. The import is: everything stated above — the Year, Month, fortnight, Day-and-Night — was all stated as being useful (upayogita) for answering that question, but none of it was the direct primary topic (sākṣāt prakṛta). The primary topic now returns: Prajāpati established as food in the form of rice, barley, and the like — from which creatures are born.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ರಯಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "Rayi as before" ।

ರಯಿಃ — Rayi · ಅನ್ನಂ — food · ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ — the Moon · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಅಹ್ನಃ — of the day · ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಉಕ್ತಿ-ಪ್ರಸಂಗಾತ್ — by occasion of / incidentally from the statement of the day's Prāṇa-nature · ಅಹ್ನಿ — by day / in the daytime · ಮೈಥುನಂ — intercourse · ಣಿಷೇಧತಿ — prohibits · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "prāṇam (Prāṇa)" ।

ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಇತಿ — on the word "prakṛtam (the main topic)" ।

ಕುತಃ ಹ ವಾ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ — "from where indeed are these creatures born?" · ಇತಿ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ — thus what was asked (at the beginning) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಪೂರ್ವೋಕ್ತಂ ಸರ್ವಂ — everything stated above · ಏತತ್ — this · ಉಪಯೋಗಿತಯಾ — as being useful / as a means · ಉಕ್ತಂ — was stated · ನ ತು — but not · ಸಾಕ್ಷಾತ್ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ — the direct primary topic · ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ — this is the import ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Applies the Rayi-Prāṇa analysis to the Day-and-Night; night is Rayi, day is Prāṇa; daytime intercourse wastes Prāṇa; nighttime union in season is brahmacarya ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Continues the fractal descent (Year → Month → Day-and-Night); identifies the prohibition and injunction as prāsaṅgika (incidental); identifies the primary topic as Prajāpati as food (rice, barley etc.) from which creatures are born ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Clarifies Rayi = food = Moon; explains the prohibition as arising from the incidental occasion of stating the day's Prāṇa-nature; most importantly identifies "prakṛtam" as pointing back to the original question of the Praśna — the primary topic is how creatures are born, and everything from the Year onwards was preparatory context (upayogita) for that answer

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The fractal descent is complete — Year → Month → Fortnight → Day-and-Night. At every level, Rayi and Prāṇa are the two aspects of Prajāpati.
  2. Day = Prāṇa = fire = eater; Night = Rayi = Moon = food. The daytime is the consuming, active principle; the night is the nourishing, material principle.
  3. The prohibition and injunction are prāsaṅgika — incidental, not primary. Śaṅkara is careful to distinguish what is directly relevant to the main topic from what arises as a contextual aside.
  4. The primary topic (prakṛtam) now returns — the original question of the Praśna: from what are creatures born? Prajāpati as food (rice, barley etc.) is the answer. Everything from the Year analysis was upayogita — useful context, not the direct answer.
  5. Ānandagiri's key contribution is pinpointing "prakṛtam" as the structural signal that Śaṅkara is now returning to the original question after the long Rayi-Prāṇa analysis — tying the entire philosophical excursus back to its starting point.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ಹ ಸ ಋಷಿರುವಾಚ ಭೂಯ ಏವ ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ಪೃಚ್ಛತ ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ ೨ ॥ To them, the sage said: "Live here for one more year, practicing austerity, brahmacarya, and faith. Then ask questions according to your desire. If we know the answers, we shall explain everything to you."

ತಾನ್ ಹ — to them indeed

  • ತಾನ್ → to them
  • ಹ → indeed

ಸ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ — the sage said

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯ ಏವ — for some more time; further

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additional
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ — through austerity, brahmacarya, and faith

  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya
  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ — you shall stay for a year

  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ → for one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay, dwell

ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ — ask questions according to your desire

  • ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ — if we know

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ — we shall indeed tell you everything

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall tell

ಇತಿ — thus

  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ ಏವಮುಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ — ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ, ತಥಾಪೀಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತೋ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ । ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯೋ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಸ್ತಮನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ । ಯದಿ ತದ್ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ । ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥೋ ಯದಿ - ಶಬ್ದೋ ನಾಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾದವಸೀಯತೇ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ To those who had approached him in that manner, the sage indeed said again: "Although you are already practitioners of austerity, nevertheless, remain here for a year with discipline — practicing austerity in the form of control of the senses, especially brahmacarya, and faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the authority of the scriptures and the teacher. Live here with reverence and with wholehearted dedication to serving the teacher. Thereafter, ask questions according to your respective desires. Whatever subject each of you wishes to know, and whatever inquiry arises in each one's mind, ask questions concerning that very subject. If we know the answer to what you ask, we shall explain it to you." The word 'if' (yadi) is used only to indicate the sage's humility and freedom from arrogance; it is not intended to imply ignorance or doubt. This is evident from the fact that all the questions are subsequently answered and resolved. Thus he says: "We shall indeed explain to you everything concerning the matters that you ask."

ತಾನ್ ಏವಮ್ ಉಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ

The sage indeed said to those who had approached him in this manner.

  • ತಾನ್ → those (students)
  • ಏವಮ್ → thus, in this manner
  • ಉಪಗತಾನ್ → those who had approached
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ ಕಿಲ → indeed
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ

Further, once again.

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additionally
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಏವ → indeed

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ

Although you are already practitioners of austerity,

  • ಯದ್ಯಪಿ → although
  • ಯೂಯಂ → you
  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → previously, already
  • ತಪಸ್ವಿನಃ → practitioners of austerity
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಥಾಪಿ ಇಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ

Even so, here through tapas, namely control of the senses,

  • ತಥಾಪಿ → nevertheless
  • ಇಹ → here
  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ-ಸಂಯಮೇನ → through restraint of the senses
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ → senses
  • ಸಂಯಮ → control, restraint
  • ಏನ → by, through

Śaṅkara explicitly glosses tapas here as indriya-saṃyama (sense-control).

ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ

Especially through brahmacarya.

  • ವಿಶೇಷತಃ → especially, particularly
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya

ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ

And through faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the scriptures and teacher.

  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith
  • ಚ → and
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ-ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ → through an attitude of trust in the authority of the scriptures
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ → faith in the validity of the Veda
  • ಬುದ್ಧಿ → understanding, attitude

ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live here for a year with reverence.

  • ಆದರ-ವಂತಃ → possessed of reverence
  • ಆದರ → respect, reverence
  • ವಂತಃ → possessing
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ → for the period of one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay

ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತಃ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live devoted to proper service of the teacher.

  • ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ → properly
  • ಗುರು-ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ-ಪರಾಃ → devoted to service of the teacher
  • ಗುರು → teacher
  • ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ → service, attendance
  • ಪರಾಃ → dedicated to
  • ಸಂತಃ → being
  • ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall live

ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ

Thereafter, according to your desire,

  • ತತಃ → then, thereafter
  • ಯಥಾ-ಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish

ಯಃ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಃ ತಂ ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ

Without going beyond what each one desires to know.

  • ಯಃ → whichever
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಕಾಮಃ → desire
  • ತಂ → that
  • ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ → not transgressing, not exceeding

ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ

Regarding whatever subject each one has an inquiry,

  • ಯದ್-ವಿಷಯೇ → regarding whichever topic
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ → desire to know, inquiry

ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ

Ask questions concerning those subjects.

  • ತದ್-ವಿಷಯಾನ್ → concerning those subjects
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ತತ್ ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ

If we know that which is asked by you,

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್-ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked by you
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ → by you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ

The word "if" is used to indicate absence of arrogance.

  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ-ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ → for demonstrating humility
  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ → non-arrogance, humility
  • ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನ → showing
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → purpose
  • ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ → the word "if"

This is an important observation of Śaṅkara.

ನ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ

It is not intended to suggest ignorance or doubt.

  • ನ → not
  • ಅಜ್ಞಾನ → ignorance
  • ಸಂಶಯ → doubt
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → meaning, purpose
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ ಅವಸೀಯತೇ

This is understood from the subsequent resolution of the questions.

  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ → from the determination of the questions
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ → questions
  • ನಿರ್ಣಯ → ascertainment, resolution
  • ಅವಸೀಯತೇ → is understood, is concluded

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ ಇತಿ

"We shall indeed explain to you everything that you ask."

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ-ಅರ್ಥಂ → the matter asked about
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ → asked
  • ಅರ್ಥಂ → subject matter
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall explain
  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.text:
ಅಥ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಭಗವನ್ಕುತೋ ಹ ವಾ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತ ಇತಿ ॥ ೩ ॥ Then Kabandhī Kātyāyana approached the teacher and asked: "O Revered Sir, from where indeed are these beings born?"

ಅಥ — then

  • ಅಥ → then, thereafter

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ — Kabandhī, the son of Kātyāyana

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhī
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana

ಉಪೇತ್ಯ — having approached

  • ಉಪೇತ್ಯ → having approached, having come near

ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ — asked

  • ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ → asked, inquired

ಭಗವನ್ — O Revered Sir

  • ಭಗವನ್ → O venerable one, revered teacher

ಕುತಃ ಹ ವಾ — from where indeed

  • ಕುತಃ → from where
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಾ → verily, surely

ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ — these beings, creatures

  • ಇಮಾಃ → these
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings, living creatures, progeny

ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ — are born

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ → are produced, are born

ಇತಿ — thus

  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಅಥ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ — ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್ , ಕುತಃ ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ ಇಮಾಃ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ । ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋರ್ಯತ್ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಸ್ತದ್ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ತದರ್ಥೋಽಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ ॥ Then, after the completion of the year, Kabandhī Kātyāyana approached the teacher and asked: "O Revered Sir, from what cause indeed are these beings, beginning with the brāhmaṇas, born?" This question is intended to elicit an explanation of the result and destination attained through the combined pursuit of aparā vidyā (lower knowledge) and karma (Vedic rituals).

ಅಥ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ

Then, after the completion of the year,

  • ಅಥ → then
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ → from the year, after the year
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → afterwards, subsequently

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ

Kabandhī Kātyāyana, having approached the teacher,

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhī
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana
  • ಉಪೇತ್ಯ → having approached
  • ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ → having come near

Śaṅkara uses both expressions simply to emphasize respectful approach to the teacher.

ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್

Asked, inquired

  • ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ → asked
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ → one who questioned

ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್

O Revered Sir,

  • ಹೇ → O!
  • ಭಗವನ್ → venerable master

ಕುತಃ ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ

From what cause indeed?

  • ಕುತಃ → from where
  • ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ → from what cause
  • ಹ ವೈ → indeed, verily

Śaṅkara glosses ಕುತಃ with ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್, making it clear that the inquiry concerns the cause of creation.

ಇಮಾಃ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ

These beings, beginning with the brāhmaṇas,

  • ಇಮಾಃ → these
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣ-ಆದ್ಯಾಃ → beginning with the brāhmaṇas
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣ → brāhmaṇa
  • ಆದ್ಯಾಃ → and others, beginning with
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → creatures, beings

Here "brāhmaṇas and others" stands for all embodied beings.

ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ

Are born, come into existence

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ → are born
  • ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ → arise, are produced

The second word is explanatory of the first.

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ

Of aparā vidyā and karma taken together,

  • ಅಪರ-ವಿದ್ಯಾ → lower knowledge (primarily Vedic learning)
  • ಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ → of karma
  • ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ → when combined together

This is a very important phrase.

ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ

What result is produced,

  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಕಾರ್ಯಂ → effect, result

ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ

What destination is attained,

  • ಯಾ → what
  • ಗತಿಃ → destination, course, attainment

ತತ್ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಇತಿ

That is what is to be explained.

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ → should be explained
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ತದರ್ಥಃ ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ

Such is the intention of this question.

  • ತದರ್ಥಃ → having that purpose
  • ಅಯಂ → this
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ → question

Important Bhāṣya Point

At first glance, Kabandhī appears to be asking a simple cosmological question:

"From where are beings born?"

But Śaṅkara sees a deeper intention.

The question is really:

"What is the origin, result, and destination of the world experienced by those who pursue Vedic learning and ritual action?"

In other words, the inquiry is not merely about physical birth. It is about the creation-order (sṛṣṭi) that forms the field in which karma operates and produces results.

Therefore Śaṅkara remarks:

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ

"The question seeks to know the result and destination associated with the combined pursuit of aparā vidyā and karma."

This prepares the way for Pippalāda's answer concerning Prajāpati, Rayi, and Prāṇa, which explains the cosmic order governing worldly existence.

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸ ಹೋವಾಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸ ತಪೋಽತಪ್ಯತ ಸ ತಪಸ್ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚೇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ॥ ೪ ॥ To him, the sage replied: "Prajāpati, desiring progeny, performed austerity. Having practiced austerity, he produced a pair — Rayi and Prāṇa — thinking, 'These two will create many kinds of beings for me.'"

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸಃ ಹ ಉವಾಚ

To him indeed he said

  • ತಸ್ಮೈ → to him

ಸಃ ತಪಃ ಅತಪ್ಯತ

He practiced austerity

  • ಅತಪ್ಯತ → practiced austerity

ಸಃ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ

ಸಃ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ

He produced a pair

  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ → produced, created

ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ

Rayi and Prāṇa

  • ರಯಿಂ → Rayi
  • ಚ → and
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa
  • ಚ → and

ಇತಿ ಏತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ

"These two will create many kinds of beings for me"

ಇತಿ

Thus

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಏವಂ ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ ಸ ಹ ಉವಾಚ ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯಾಹ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನಃ ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ ವೈ, ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್ ಜಗತ್ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮೀತ್ಯೇವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತೋ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ, ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ , ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತಾರ್ಥವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ, ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ । ಅಥ ತು ಸಃ ಏವಂ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಶ್ರೌತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಮನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ, ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ಮಿಥುನಂ ದ್ವಂದ್ವಮುತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಸೋಮಮನ್ನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಅಗ್ನಿಮತ್ತಾರಮ್ ಇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ ಅತ್ರನ್ನಭೂತೌ ಮೇ ಮಮ ಬಹುಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಸೂರ್ಯಾಚಂದ್ರಮಸಾವಕಲ್ಪಯತ್ ॥ To him who had asked in this manner, Pippalāda replied in order to remove his doubt. Prajāpati, desiring to create beings from himself, being the Self of all and endowed with the knowledge, "I shall create the universe," and acting in accordance with that knowledge, manifested as Hiraṇyagarbha at the beginning of a cycle of creation. As the lord of all beings that were to be created, both stationary and moving, he contemplated upon tapas, which here means knowledge concerning the truths revealed by the scriptures and carried forward from previous births. Having thus practiced that tapas, and having reflected upon the scriptural knowledge, he created a pair which would serve as the means of creation. He produced the duality of Rayi and Prāṇa — Rayi being the Moon, food; and Prāṇa being Fire, the eater of food. Thinking, "These two, Agni and Soma, food and eater, will generate for me beings in many forms," he projected the Sun and Moon through the process of cosmic manifestation beginning from the cosmic egg.

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಏವಂ ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ

To him who had asked in this manner

  • ತಸ್ಮೈ → to him
  • ಏವಂ → thus, in this manner
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ → to the one who had questioned

ಸಃ ಹ ಉವಾಚ

He indeed said

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯ

For removing that doubt

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅಪಾಕರಣಾಯ → for removal, for clearing away

ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನಃ ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ

Desiring to create beings from himself

  • ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಕಾಮಃ → desirous of creating beings
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings
  • ಆತ್ಮನಃ → from himself (panchami vibhakthi)
  • ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ → desirous of creating

ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ

Indeed Prajāpati

  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ → Prajāpati

ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್

Being the Self of all

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಆತ್ಮಾ → Self
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಜಗತ್ ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಇತಿ

"I shall create the universe"

  • ಜಗತ್ → universe
  • ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ → I shall create
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ಏವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್

Possessed of this knowledge

  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ → endowed with knowledge

ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ

Acting in accordance with that knowledge

  • ಯಥಾ → according to
  • ಉಕ್ತ → what was known or understood
  • ಕಾರೀ → one who acts

ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ

Endowed with that contemplation

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಭಾವ → contemplation, idea
  • ಭಾವಿತಃ → imbued with, pervaded by

ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ

Manifested as Hiraṇyagarbha at the beginning of creation

  • ಕಲ್ಪ-ಆದೌ → at the beginning of a kalpa
  • ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ → manifested, came forth
  • ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ → Hiraṇyagarbha

ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್

Being the lord of all beings to be created, moving and unmoving

  • ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ → of those being created
  • ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ → beings
  • ಸ್ಥಾವರ → stationary
  • ಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ → moving
  • ಪತಿಃ → lord
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ

Knowledge carried over from previous births

  • ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರ → previous births
  • ಭಾವಿತಂ → cultivated, carried forward
  • ಜ್ಞಾನಂ → knowledge

ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತಾರ್ಥವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ

Tapas consisting of knowledge of truths revealed by scripture

  • ಶ್ರುತಿ → scripture
  • ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತ → revealed
  • ಅರ್ಥ → truth, meaning
  • ವಿಷಯಂ → concerning
  • ತಪಃ → tapas

ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ

He reflected upon; he practiced tapas

  • ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ → contemplated
  • ಅತಪ್ಯತ → practiced tapas

ಅಥ ತು ಸಃ ಏವಂ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ

Then, having thus performed tapas

  • ಅಥ ತು → then indeed
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ತಪಃ → tapas
  • ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ → having practiced

ಶ್ರೌತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ

Having reflected upon scriptural knowledge

  • ಶ್ರೌತಂ → scriptural (told in the vedas)
  • ಜ್ಞಾನಂ → knowledge
  • ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ → having contemplated

ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ

He produced a pair that would become the means of creation

  • ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ → creation
  • ಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ → serving as the means
  • ಮಿಥುನಂ → pair (duality)
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ → produced

ಮಿಥುನಂ ದ್ವಂದ್ವಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್

He created a duality

  • ಮಿಥುನಂ → pair
  • ದ್ವಂದ್ವಂ → duality
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ → created

ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಸೋಮಮ್ ಅನ್ನಂ

Rayi, namely the Moon, which is food

  • ರಯಿಂ → Rayi
  • ಚ → and
  • ಸೋಮಂ → Moon (in the form of food)
  • ಅನ್ನಂ → food

ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಅಗ್ನಿಮ್ ಅತ್ತಾರಮ್

Prāṇa, namely Fire, the eater

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa (in the form of fire)
  • ಚ → and
  • ಅಗ್ನಿಂ → Fire
  • ಅತ್ತಾರಂ → eater, consumer

ಇತಿ ಏತೌ ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ

Thus these two are Agni and Soma

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏತೌ → these two
  • ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ → Agni and Soma

ಅನ್ನಭೂತೌ

Food and eater (TODO CHECK) - Athru -> here --- CHECK - ಅನ್ನ → food - ಭೂತೌ → being

ಮೇ ಮಮ ಬಹುಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ

Will create for me beings of many kinds

  • ಮೇ / ಮಮ → for me
  • ಬಹುಧಾ → manifoldly
  • ಅನೇಕಧಾ → in many ways
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings
  • ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ → will create

ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ

Having thus thought

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏವಂ → in this manner
  • ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ → having reflected

ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ

Through the process of cosmic egg manifestation

  • ಅಂಡ → cosmic egg
  • ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿ → origination
  • ಕ್ರಮೇಣ → in sequence

ಸೂರ್ಯಾಚಂದ್ರಮಸೌ ಅಕಲ್ಪಯತ್

He projected the Sun and Moon

  • ಸೂರ್ಯ → Sun
  • ಚಂದ್ರಮಸೌ → Moon
  • ಅಕಲ್ಪಯತ್ → projected, brought forth

docs.text: ಆದಿತ್ಯೋ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ರಯಿರೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ರಯಿರ್ವಾ ಏತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ಯನ್ಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚಾಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ತಸ್ಮಾನ್ಮೂರ್ತಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ॥ ೫ ॥   The Sun indeed is Prāṇa, and the Moon indeed is Rayi. Verily, all this—whatever is formed and whatever is formless—is Rayi. Therefore, form alone is Rayi.

docs.text:
ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ

  • ವೈ → verily, indeed

  • ಏವ → indeed

  • ಚ → and

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ತತ್ರ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ । ರಯಿರೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ । ರಯಿರೇವಾನ್ನಂ ಸೋಮ ಏವ । ತದೇತದೇಕಮತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಶ್ಚಾನ್ನಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿರೇಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ; ಗುಣಪ್ರಧಾನಕೃತೋ ಭೇದಃ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ರಯಿರ್ವೈ ಅನ್ನಮೇವ ಏತತ್ ಸರ್ವಮ್ । ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ? ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸ್ಥೂಲಂ ಚ ಅಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮಂ ಚ । ಮೂರ್ತಾಮೂರ್ತೇ ಅತ್ತ್ರನ್ನರೂಪೇ ಅಪಿ ರಯಿರೇವ । ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಭಕ್ತಾದಮೂರ್ತಾತ್ ಯದನ್ಯನ್ಮೂರ್ತರೂಪಂ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ, ಸೈವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್ ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ॥   Among the two, the Sun is indeed Prāṇa, the eater, Fire. The Moon alone is Rayi. Rayi itself is food, that is, Soma.  Thus, the eater, Fire, and the food together constitute a single Prajāpati appearing as a pair. The distinction between them is made only on account of differences in attributes and predominance.  How so? Indeed, all this is nothing but Rayi, that is, food. What is that all? Whatever is gross and formed, and whatever is subtle and formless. Both the formed and the formless, though constituting the eater and the eaten, are still Rayi alone.  Therefore, among these, the formed aspect, distinguished from the formless, is specifically called Rayi or food, because it is consumed by the formless eater.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ತತ್ರ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ

The eater, namely Fire

Rayi itself is food, namely Soma

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚ

The eater, Fire, and the food are one

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಏಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಮ್

How?

ರಯಿಃ ವೈ ಅನ್ನಂ ಏವ ಏತತ್ ಸರ್ವಮ್

Indeed all this is nothing but food (Rayi)

What is that all?

ಮೂರ್ತಾಮೂರ್ತೇ ಅತ್ತ್ರನ್ನರೂಪೇ ಅಪಿ

Though existing as eater and eaten

  • ಅತ್ತ್ರನ್ನ-ರೂಪೇ → in the form of eater and food

ರಯಿಃ ಏವ

They are still Rayi alone

  • ಏವ → alone

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್

Therefore

  • ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ → therefore

ಪ್ರವಿಭಕ್ತಾತ್ ಅಮೂರ್ತಾತ್

Separated from the formless aspect

  • ಅಮೂರ್ತಾತ್ → from the formless

ಯತ್ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತರೂಪಂ

That which is the formed aspect

ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಸಾ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್

That form alone is called Rayi, food

  • ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ → form
  • ಸಾ ಏವ → that alone

ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್

Because it is consumed by the formless eater

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಅಥಾದಿತ್ಯ ಉದಯನ್ಯತ್ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ತೇನ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ । ಯದ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ ಯದುದೀಚೀಂ ಯದಧೋ ಯದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಯದಂತರಾ ದಿಶೋ ಯತ್ಸರ್ವಂ, ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ ತೇನ, ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ॥ ೬ ॥   Then, when the Sun rises and enters the eastern direction, by that he gathers the beings of the east into his rays. Likewise, when he illumines the southern, western, northern, lower, upper, and intermediate directions—indeed all directions—by that he gathers all beings into his rays.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಉದಯನ್

Then the Sun, rising

  • ಅಥ → then
  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ → the Sun
  • ಉದಯನ್ → rising

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ

When he enters the eastern direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ → eastern
  • ದಿಶಂ → direction
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ → enters

ತೇನ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್

By that, the beings of the east

  • ತೇನ → by that
  • ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ → those in the east
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ → living beings

ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ

He places in his rays

  • ರಶ್ಮಿಷು → in the rays
  • ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ → gathers, places, establishes

ಯತ್ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ

When (he illumines) the southern direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ → southern direction

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ

When (he illumines) the western direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ → western direction

ಯತ್ ಉದೀಚೀಂ

When (he illumines) the northern direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಉದೀಚೀಂ → northern direction

ಯತ್ ಅಧಃ

When (he illumines) below

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಅಧಃ → below

ಯತ್ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ

When (he illumines) above

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → above

ಯತ್ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ

When (he illumines) the intermediate directions

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಅಂತರಾ → intermediate
  • ದಿಶಃ → directions

ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ

When he illumines all

  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಸರ್ವಂ → all
  • ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ → illumines

ತೇನ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್

By that, all beings

  • ತೇನ → by that
  • ಸರ್ವಾನ್ → all
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ → living beings

ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ

He gathers into his rays

  • ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ → gathers, places, establishes

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ತಥಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತೋಽಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽತ್ತಾ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಯಚ್ಚಾದ್ಯಮ್ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಉದಯನ್ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಗೋಚರಮಾಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಯತ್ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾವಭಾಸರೂಪೇಷು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ಕರೋತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ತಥೈವ ಯತ್ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ ಯದುದೀಚೀಮ್ ಅಧಃ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ಯಚ್ಚ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ ಕೋಣದಿಶೋಽವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ ಯಚ್ಚಾನ್ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್ಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ॥   Likewise, though Prāṇa is formless, it is the eater of everything that is fit to be eaten.  How is this so?  When the Sun rises and becomes visible to the eyes of living beings, and enters or pervades the eastern direction through its own light, by that pervasion it gathers into its rays all beings dwelling in the east, who are in the nature of food. Since the rays are pervaded by the Sun's own luminous presence, the beings are established in them. That is, the Sun makes them one with himself.  Similarly, when he pervades the southern, western, northern, lower, upper, and intermediate directions, and indeed whatever else he illumines, by that all-pervading light he gathers into his rays all beings dwelling in every direction.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ತಥಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ

Likewise, though Prāṇa is formless, it is the eater

  • ತಥಾ → likewise
  • ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ → formless
  • ಅಪಿ → though
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಅತ್ತಾ → eater, consumer

ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಯತ್ ಚ ಆದ್ಯಮ್

Of everything that is fit to be eaten

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಚ → and
  • ಆದ್ಯಮ್ → fit to be eaten, edible

ಕಥಮ್

How?

  • ಕಥಮ್ → how

ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಉದಯನ್ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್

Then the Sun, rising and ascending

  • ಅಥ → then
  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ → the Sun
  • ಉದಯನ್ → rising
  • ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್ → ascending

ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಗೋಚರಂ ಆಗಚ್ಛನ್

Coming within the range of vision of living beings

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ → of living beings
  • ಚಕ್ಷುಃ-ಗೋಚರಂ → within the field of vision
  • ಆಗಚ್ಛನ್ → coming

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ

When he enters and pervades the eastern direction by his own light

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ → eastern
  • ದಿಶಂ → direction
  • ಸ್ವ-ಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ → by his own light
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ → enters
  • ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ → pervades

ತೇನ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ

By that pervasion of himself

  • ತೇನ → by that
  • ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮ-ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ → through his own pervasion

ಸರ್ವಾಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್

All beings dwelling therein

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಅಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ → dwelling within
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ → living beings

ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ ಅನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್

Those in the east, who are food

  • ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ → eastern beings
  • ಅನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್ → being in the nature of food

ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾವಭಾಸರೂಪೇಷು

Into the rays, which are manifestations of his own light

  • ರಶ್ಮಿಷು → into the rays
  • ಸ್ವ-ಆತ್ಮ-ಅವಭಾಸ-ರೂಪೇಷು → having the nature of his own radiance

ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್

Because they are pervaded by him

  • ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು → pervaded
  • ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ → because of pervasion

ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ

He gathers and establishes the beings

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ → living beings
  • ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ → gathers
  • ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ → establishes

ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ ಕರೋತಿ ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ

That is, he makes them his own self

  • ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ → one with himself
  • ಕರೋತಿ → makes
  • ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ → this is the meaning

ತಥೈವ

Similarly

  • ತಥೈವ → likewise

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ

When he enters the southern direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ → enters
  • ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ → southern direction

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ

When he enters the western direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ → western direction

ಯತ್ ಉದೀಚೀಮ್

When he enters the northern direction

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಉದೀಚೀಮ್ → northern direction

ಅಧಃ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ

Below and above

  • ಅಧಃ → below
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → above

ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ

When he enters

  • ಯತ್ → when
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ → enters

ಯಚ್ಚ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ

And the intermediate directions

  • ಯತ್ ಚ → and whatever
  • ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ → intermediate directions

ಕೋಣದಿಶಃ ಅವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ

The corner directions, subsidiary directions

  • ಕೋಣದಿಶಃ → corner directions
  • ಅವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ → intermediate directions

ಯಚ್ಚ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ

And whatever else he illumines

  • ಯತ್ ಚ → and whatever
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → other
  • ಸರ್ವಂ → all
  • ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ → illumines

ತೇನ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ

By the pervasion of his own light

  • ತೇನ → by that
  • ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶ → self-luminosity
  • ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ → through pervasion

ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್ಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್

All beings dwelling in all directions

  • ಸರ್ವಾನ್ → all
  • ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್-ಸ್ಥಾನ್ → situated in all directions
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ → living beings

ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ

He gathers into his rays

  • ರಶ್ಮಿಷು → into the rays
  • ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ → gathers, establishes

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಸ ಏಷ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽಗ್ನಿರುದಯತೇ । ತದೇತದೃಚಾಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ॥ ೭ ॥   This very Prāṇa, rising as the Sun, is Vaiśvānara, the cosmic Fire, of universal form. Concerning this, the following Ṛg-vedic mantra has been declared.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಸಃ ಏಷಃ

This very one

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏಷಃ → this very one

ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ

Vaiśvānara, the universal Fire

  • ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ → the cosmic fire, Vaiśvānara

ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ

Of universal form

  • ವಿಶ್ವ → all, universe
  • ರೂಪಃ → form

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಉದಯತೇ

Prāṇa, as Fire, rises

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಅಗ್ನಿಃ → Fire
  • ಉದಯತೇ → rises

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಋಚಾ ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್

This has been declared by a Vedic verse

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಋಚಾ → by a Ṛg-vedic mantra
  • ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ → has been stated, declared

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಸ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಶ್ಚ ಸ ಏವಾತ್ತಾ ಉದಯತೇ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ । ತದೇತತ್ ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು ಋಚಾ ಮಂತ್ರೇಣಾಪಿ ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ॥   This very Prāṇa, the eater, is Vaiśvānara, the Self of all, possessing the form of the entire universe. Because he is the Self of all, Prāṇa and Fire are one and the same. That very eater rises every day, ascending while bringing all directions under his sway.  This very truth that has been explained is also declared in a Ṛg-vedic mantra.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಸಃ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ

This very Prāṇa, the eater, is Vaiśvānara

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏಷಃ → this very one
  • ಅತ್ತಾ → eater
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ → Vaiśvānara, the universal Fire

ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ

The Self of all, possessing universal form

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಆತ್ಮಾ → Self
  • ವಿಶ್ವ → universe
  • ರೂಪಃ → form

ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ ಚ

And because he is the Self of the universe

  • ವಿಶ್ವ → universe
  • ಆತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ → because of being the Self
  • ಚ → and

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ

Prāṇa and Fire

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಅಗ್ನಿಃ → Fire
  • ಚ → and

ಸಃ ಏವ ಅತ್ತಾ

That very one is the eater

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಅತ್ತಾ → eater

ಉದಯತೇ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ

Rises and ascends

  • ಉದಯತೇ → rises
  • ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ → ascends

ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ

Every day

  • ಪ್ರತಿ → each
  • ಅಹಂ → day

ಸರ್ವಾಃ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್

Bringing all directions under himself

  • ಸರ್ವಾಃ → all
  • ದಿಶಃ → directions
  • ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್-ಕುರ್ವನ್ → making his own, bringing under his control

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು

This very truth that has been taught

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಉಕ್ತಂ → spoken, taught
  • ವಸ್ತು → reality, subject matter

ಋಚಾ ಮಂತ್ರೇಣ ಅಪಿ ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್

Has also been declared by a Vedic mantra

  • ಋಚಾ → by a Ṛg-vedic verse
  • ಮಂತ್ರೇಣ → by a mantra
  • ಅಪಿ → also
  • ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ → declared, stated

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿರೇಕಂ ತಪಂತಮ್ । ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಮುದಯತ್ಯೇಷ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥ ೮ ॥   This Sun, who is the Prāṇa of all beings, rises as the one light, the ultimate refuge, all-formed, radiant, all-knowing, shining brightly, possessing a thousand rays, and manifesting himself in hundreds of ways.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ

Of universal form

  • ವಿಶ್ವ → universe, all
  • ರೂಪಂ → form

ಹರಿಣಂ

Radiant, shining

  • ಹರಿಣಂ → shining, golden-hued, radiant

ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ

The all-knowing one

  • ಜಾತ → beings, things that are born
  • ವೇದಸಂ → knower
  • ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ → knower of all beings

ಪರಾಯಣಂ

The supreme refuge

  • ಪರ → supreme
  • ಆಯಣಂ → refuge, resting place

ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಏಕಂ

The one light

  • ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ → light
  • ಏಕಂ → one

ತಪಂತಮ್

Shining, heating

  • ತಪಂತಮ್ → blazing, shining forth

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ

Possessing a thousand rays

  • ಸಹಸ್ರ → thousand
  • ರಶ್ಮಿಃ → rays

ಶತಧಾ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ

Manifesting in hundreds of ways

  • ಶತಧಾ → in a hundred ways
  • ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ → existing, functioning, manifesting

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ

The Prāṇa of all beings

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → life-principle
  • ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ → of beings

ಉದಯತಿ

Rises

  • ಉದಯತಿ → rises

ಏಷಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ

This Sun

  • ಏಷಃ → this
  • ಸೂರ್ಯಃ → the Sun

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ರಶ್ಮಿವಂತಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾಶ್ರಯಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಭೂತಮ್ ಏಕಮ್ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ ತಪಂತಂ ತಾಪಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ । ಕೋಽಸೌ ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ? ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಮ್ ಉದಯತಿ ಏಷಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥   The knowers of Brahman understand the Sun as their very Self — the one who has all forms, who is radiant with rays, who knows all beings, who is the refuge of all, who is the light, who serves as the eye of all living beings, who is one without a second, and who shines by performing the function of giving heat and light.  Who is that Sun whom they thus realize?  He is the one possessing countless rays, manifesting in many ways through the diversity of living beings. This very Sun rises as the Prāṇa, the life-principle of all creatures.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ

Having all forms, possessing the form of the entire universe

  • ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ → of universal form
  • ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ → possessing all forms

ಹರಿಣಂ ರಶ್ಮಿವಂತಂ

Radiant and endowed with rays

  • ಹರಿಣಂ → shining, radiant (kirana- rays)
  • ರಶ್ಮಿವಂತಂ → possessed of rays

ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ

The knower of all beings

  • ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ → knower of all that is born (prajnana)
  • ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ → aware of all creatures

ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾಶ್ರಯಂ

The supreme refuge and support of all beings

  • ಪರಾಯಣಂ → ultimate refuge
  • ಸರ್ವ-ಪ್ರಾಣ-ಆಶ್ರಯಂ → support of all living beings

ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಭೂತಮ್

The light that serves as the eye of all creatures

  • ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ → light
  • ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ → of all living beings
  • ಚಕ್ಷುಃ-ಭೂತಮ್ → functioning as the eye (abhimani devata)

ಏಕಮ್ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ

One without a second

  • ಏಕಮ್ → one
  • ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ → without a second

ತಪಂತಂ ತಾಪಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ

Shining and performing the act of heating

  • ತಪಂತಂ → shining, blazing
  • ತಾಪ-ಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ → the act of heating
  • ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ → performing

ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ

The Sun as one's own Self

  • ಸ್ವ-ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → one's own Self
  • ಸೂರ್ಯಂ → the Sun (jnanis)

ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ

The knowers of Brahman have realized

  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ → have known, realized
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ → knowers of Brahman

ಕಃ ಅಸೌ ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ

Who is that whom they have realized?

  • ಕಃ → who
  • ಅಸೌ → that
  • ಯಂ → whom
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ → have realized

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ

Possessing countless rays

  • ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ → thousand-rayed
  • ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ → having many rays

ಶತಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ

Manifesting in many ways

  • ಶತಧಾ → in hundreds of ways
  • ಅನೇಕಧಾ → in many ways

ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ

Existing through the diversity of living beings

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಿ → living being
  • ಭೇದೇನ → through distinctions
  • ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ → manifesting, existing

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ

The life-principle of all creatures

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ → of beings

ಉದಯತಿ ಏಷಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ

This Sun rises

  • ಉದಯತಿ → rises
  • ಏಷಃ → this
  • ಸೂರ್ಯಃ → the Sun

docs.title: Praśna Upaniṣad — First Question, Verse 9
docs.text: Source of Ṭīkā: Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series No. 8 (Ānandagiri on Śaṅkara Bhāṣya)

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ತದಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತೇ ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಲೋಕಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

ತ ಏವ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿರ್ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Year (Saṃvatsara) is indeed Prajāpati (the Lord of creatures). His two paths are the Southern and the Northern. Those who worship iṣṭa (sacrificial rites) and pūrta (charitable works) as the (sufficient) accomplishment — they win only the lunar world. They indeed return again (to this world). Therefore those seers who desire progeny resort to the Southern path. This very Pitṛyāṇa is Rayi (the material/nourishing principle).

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — the Year · ವೈ — indeed / verily · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — Lord of creatures · ತಸ್ಯ — his · ಅಯನೇ — in the paths / solstice-courses · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ — the Southern (path) · ಚ — and · ಉತ್ತರಂ — the Northern (path) · ಚ — and ।

ತತ್ — that · ಯೇ — those who · ಹ ವೈ — truly / indeed · ತತ್ — that (qualifying the action) · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ — sacrificial rites and charitable works · ಕೃತಂ — accomplished / done · ಇತಿ — thus (thinking) · ಉಪಾಸತೇ — they worship · ತೇ — they · ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಂ ಏವ — only the lunar · ಲೋಕಂ — world / realm · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — win / attain ।

ತೇ ಏವ — they indeed · ಪುನಃ — again · ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ — return · ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — therefore · ಏತೇ — these · ಋಷಯಃ — seers / sages · ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ — desirous of progeny · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ — the Southern (path) · ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ — resort to / enter upon ।

ಏಷಃ — this · ಹ ವೈ — verily / indeed · ರಯಿಃ — Rayi (the material / nourishing principle) · ಯಃ — which · ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ — the path of the ancestors ॥

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿರನ್ನಮಮೂರ್ತಿಶ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽತ್ತಾದಿತ್ಯಸ್ತದೇತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ, ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — ತದೇವ ಕಾಲಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ, ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರಸಮುದಾಯೋ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದ್ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣೈತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವೇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ ।

ತತ್ಕಥಮ್ ? ತಸ್ಯ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಅಯನೇ ಮಾರ್ಗೌ ದ್ವೌ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹ್ಯಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನೋತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧತ್ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಚ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿಷು ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ಋಷಯಃ ತದುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ।

ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಣೋ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಸ್ತಚ್ಛಬ್ದಃ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಪೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ನಾಕೃತಂ ನಿತ್ಯಮ್, ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಸಿ ಭವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಸ್ಯಾಂಶಂ ರಯಿಮನ್ನಭೂತಂ ಲೋಕಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಸ್ಯ ।

ತೇ ಏವ ಚ ಕೃತಕ್ಷಯಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಂ ಹೀನತರಂ ವಾ ವಿಶಂತೀತಿ ಹ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾದೇವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಮನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನಾಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸ್ವಕೃತಮೇವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್, ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಶ್ಚಂದ್ರಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
[Opening question — pūrvapakṣa:] The Moon is what has form (mūrti); food is matter; the formless (amūrti) is Prāṇa; and the Sun is the eater — how can this one pair generate all progeny?

[Answer:] It is said thus: That very Kāla (Time) is the Saṃvatsara, and the Saṃvatsara is indeed Prajāpati — because everything is produced out of it. For the Year is nothing but the aggregate of tithis (lunar days), days, and nights, produced by Moon and Sun together. Since the Year is non-different from the dyad of Rayi and Prāṇa, it is said to be of the very nature of that pair (mithunātmaka).

How so? Prajāpati the Year has two paths — the Southern and the Northern. These are the well-known solstices (ayanas), each characterised by six months, by which the Sun (Savitṛ) travels southward and northward, distributing worlds respectively to those who perform only ritual action (kevalakarmins) and to those who combine knowledge with action (jñānasaṃyuktakarmavants).

How exactly? Among Brāhmaṇas and others — those seers who worship the iṣṭāpūrta as accomplished. The second occurrence of the word "tat" here serves as an adjective qualifying the action. Iṣṭa is sacrificial rite; pūrta is charitable work (and so on); they worship only what has been done (kṛtam) — not what is eternal and unconditioned (nitya). They win only the cāndramasa (lunar) world — the Rayi portion, the food-natured, material aspect of Prajāpati's dyadic nature, which exists in the Moon — because the lunar world has the character of the accomplished (kṛtarūpa).

They indeed return again when their accumulated merit is exhausted — entering this world or a still lower one, as has been stated. Because those seers — householders and perceivers of heaven — desire progeny and produce Prajāpati in his food-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable rites, they resort to the Southern path signified by the Southern solstice, which is nothing but the result of their own deeds. This Pitṛyāṇa is verily Rayi — food/matter. The Moon, characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa path, is that Rayi.

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ — produced by Moon and Sun · ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರಸಮುದಾಯಃ — aggregate of lunar days, days, and nights · ಹಿ — for / indeed · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — the Year · ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because of non-difference from that · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ — Rayi (matter) and Prāṇa (life-force) · ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ — of the very nature of that pair · ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — thus it is said ।

ತತ್ ಕಥಮ್ — how so? · ತಸ್ಯ — of him · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ — of Prajāpati · ಅಯನೇ — paths / courses · ಮಾರ್ಗೌ ದ್ವೌ — two paths · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚ ಉತ್ತರಂ ಚ — Southern and Northern ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ — well-known · ಹಿ — indeed · ಅಯನೇ — solstice / course · ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಲಕ್ಷಣೇ — characterised by six months · ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ — by which two · ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ — by the Southern · ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ — and by the Northern · ಯಾತಿ — travels / moves · ಸವಿತಾ — the Sun · ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ — of those who perform only ritual action · ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ — of those who combine knowledge with action · ಚ — and · ಲೋಕಾನ್ — worlds · ವಿದಧತ್ — distributing / allotting ।

ಕಥಮ್ — how? · ತತ್ — that · ತತ್ರ — there / among them · ಚ — and · ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿಷು — among Brāhmaṇas and others · ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ಋಷಯಃ — those seers indeed who · ತತ್ ಉಪಾಸತೇ — worship that · ಇತಿ — thus ।

ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಣಃ — adjective qualifying the action · ದ್ವಿತೀಯಃ — the second · ತಚ್ಛಬ್ದಃ — occurrence of the word "tat" ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ — sacrificial rite (offering into fire) · ಚ — and · ಪೂರ್ತಂ — charitable work (digging wells etc.) · ಚ — and · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ — iṣṭa and pūrta together · ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ — and so on · ಕೃತಂ ಏವ — only what has been done · ಉಪಾಸತೇ — they worship · ನ ಅಕೃತಂ ನಿತ್ಯಂ — not the unconditioned / eternal · ತೇ — they · ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಂ ಏವ — only the lunar · ಚಂದ್ರಮಸಿ ಭವಂ — existing in / belonging to the Moon · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ — of Prajāpati · ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಸ್ಯ ಅಂಶಂ — the portion of the dyadic one · ರಯಿಂ — Rayi (the material principle) · ಅನ್ನಭೂತಂ — that which has become food / food-natured · ಲೋಕಂ — world / realm · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — they win / attain · ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾತ್ — because of having the character of the accomplished · ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಸ್ಯ — of the lunar world ।

ತೇ ಏವ ಚ — they indeed · ಕೃತಕ್ಷಯಾತ್ — due to exhaustion of accumulated merit · ಪುನಃ ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ — return again · ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಂ — this world · ಹೀನತರಂ ವಾ — or a still lower one · ವಿಶಂತಿ — they enter · ಇತಿ ಹಿ ಉಕ್ತಂ — for thus it has been stated ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ — because · ಏವಂ — thus · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ — Prajāpati · ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ — whose nature is food · ಫಲತ್ವೇನ — as their fruit / result · ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ — they produce / bring about · ಚಂದ್ರಂ — the Moon · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತಕರ್ಮಣಾ — by means of sacrificial and charitable action · ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ — desirous of progeny · ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ — seekers of offspring · ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ — these seers · ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ — perceivers of heaven · ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ — householders · ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — therefore · ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ — nothing but the result of their own deeds · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ — the Southern (path) · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ — signified by the Southern solstice · ಚಂದ್ರಂ — the Moon · ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ — they resort to / reach ।

ಏಷಃ ಹ ವೈ — this verily · ರಯಿಃ — Rayi · ಅನ್ನಂ — food / matter · ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ — which is the Pitṛyāṇa · ಪಿತೃಯಾಣೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಃ ಚಂದ್ರಃ — the Moon characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa path ॥

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya contains four sentences whose word-order is sufficiently compressed or inverted that the syntactic structure needs to be laid out explicitly. These are the four that Ānandagiri himself flags with "ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ."

Sentence 1 — The pūrvapakṣa (opening question)

As written:

ಯಃ ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ — ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ — ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಯಃ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಅಸೌ [ಸಃ] ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ [ರಯಿಃ] ; ಅನ್ನಂ [ಅಪಿ ರಯಿಃ ಏವ] ।

ಯಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ [ಸಃ] ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ; ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ [ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಏವ,] ಅತ್ತಾ [ಚ] ।

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ [ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪಂ] ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

[ಏತತ್ ಮಿಥುನಂ] ಕಥಂ [ಸರ್ವಾಃ] ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ [ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ] ?

English: That Moon is the formed one (Rayi); food too is Rayi. That Prāṇa is the formless one; the Sun too is Prāṇa, and is the eater. That one pair — of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa — is all, is everything. [Question:] How will this pair generate all progeny?

Sentence 2 — The Year produces through tithis and ahorātras

As written:

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ।

ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಏತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ [ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಹಿ [ಕಃ ?] ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥಿ-ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ [ಏವ] ।

[ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ [ಅನನ್ಯಃ] — ತದ್-ಅನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — [ಅತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

English: For what is the Year? It is the aggregate of the tithis produced by the Moon and the ahorātras (days-and-nights) produced by the Sun. Since the Year is non-different from the Rayi-Prāṇa pair — because of that non-difference — the Year is said to be of the very nature of that pair.

Note: The compound ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ hides the internal division that Ānandagiri makes explicit: tithis are produced by the Moon, ahorātras by the Sun — not both by both.

Sentence 3 — The Sun's two movements and the worlds allotted (the most complex sentence)

As written:

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹಿ ಅಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸ-ಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order — two separate syntactic streams):

[Stream 1 — Southern path:] ಸವಿತಾ [ಚಂದ್ರಃ ಅಪಿ — ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಾತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

[Stream 2 — Northern path:] [ಸ ಏವ ಸವಿತಾ] ಉತ್ತರೇಣ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

English: Stream 1: The Sun (and the Moon too, by upalakaṣaṇa) travels by the Southern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who perform only ritual action.

Stream 2: That same Sun travels by the Northern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who combine knowledge with action.

Note: The original text runs both streams together in one participial construction (ವಿದಧತ್ governing both objects). Ānandagiri's anvaya splits them explicitly and also adds that ಸವಿತಾ is an upalakaṣaṇa — it denotes the Moon as well, since the Moon too moves along these paths generating tithis.

Sentence 4 — The final statement on householder-seers and the Southern path

As written:

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ, ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ, ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ, ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ — ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ [ಮಾಧ್ಯಮೇನ] ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಚ] ಚಂದ್ರರೂಪಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ [ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್] — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ [ತೇ] ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ [ಯತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ [ಚಂದ್ರಂ] ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

English: Because these seers — desirous of progeny, seekers of offspring, perceivers of heaven, householders — bring about Prajāpati in his food-natured Moon-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable action, therefore they resort to nothing but their own deed, which is the Southern path — the Moon indicated by the Southern solstice.

Note: The accumulation of four appositive epithets for ಋಷಯಃ and the placement of ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್…ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ across the sentence boundary makes this the densest construction in the Bhāṣya on this verse. The anvaya clarifies that ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ and ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ are the two main verbs, and that ಚಂದ್ರಂ is to be supplied in the concluding clause from context.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಪಕ್ರಾಂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮುಪಸಂಹರತಿ – ಯಶ್ಚಾಸಾವಿತಿ ।

ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಯಶ್ಚಾಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಮಿತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಏತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ ತತ್ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಕಾರೇಣೇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಉಚ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ।

ತದೇವ ಮಿಥುನಮೇವ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಃ ।

ಸ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕಮಿಥುನನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ತದುಪಪಾದಯತಿ – ಚಂದ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾಸ್ತಿಥಯ ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾನ್ಯಹೋತ್ರಾಣೀತಿ ವಿಭಾಗಃ ।

ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇಽಪಿ ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ ಕಥಂ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತೇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣಯೋರಭೇದಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ನ ಕೇವಲಂ ತಿಥ್ಯಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಕಿಂ ತ್ವಯನದ್ವಯದ್ವಾರಾಽಪೀತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯಂ ತತ್ಪ್ರಶ್ನಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ತತ್ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಕುತೋ ಹೇತ್ವಂತರಾದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಯಾತಿ ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದುತ್ತರೇಣ ಯಾತೀತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಸವಿತೇತ್ಯುಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ।

ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಾದಿರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷಾದಿರುತ್ತರಾಯಣಮಿತಿ ಶ್ರುತಿಷು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ ತತಶ್ಚ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿಧಾತುಂ ತಯೋರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಗಮನಾತ್ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಯನದ್ವಯಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಸ್ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ತಯೋರಯನಯೋರಿತಿ ತದ್ದ್ವಾರಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಯೋಃ ಕಥಂ ಲೋಕವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಯಣದ್ವಾರಾ ಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲೋಕಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ತಯೋಸ್ತದ್ವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯೇನ ಪರಿಹರತಿ – ತತ್ತತ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚೇತಿ ।

ಅಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ ತಪಃ ಸತ್ಯಂ ವೇದಾನಾಂ ಚಾನುಪಾಲನಮ್ ।

ಆತಿಥ್ಯಂ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಶ್ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ವಾಪೀಕೂಪತಡಾಗಾದಿ ದೇವತಾಯತನಾನಿ ಚ ।

ಅನ್ನಪ್ರದಾನಮಾರಾಮಃ ಪೂರ್ತಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ಇತಿ ತಯೋರ್ಭೇದಃ ।

ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ಕೃತಶಬ್ದೋಪರಿತನಮಿತಿಶಬ್ದಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೂರ್ತಶಬ್ದೋಪರ್ಯಾಕೃಷ್ಯಾಽಽದಿಶಬ್ದಪರ್ಯಾಯತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಇತ್ಯಾದೀತಿ ।

ದತ್ತಮಾದಿಶಬ್ದಾರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ಕಾರ್ಯಮೇವಾನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇದಂ ಚ ವಿಶೇಷಣಂ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಹೇತುತಯೋಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಕೃತರೂಪೇಷ್ಟ್ಯಾದಿಜನ್ಯತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಕೃತತ್ವೇನಾನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿರಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಮಂತ್ರವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಮಾಣಯತಿ – ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಮಿತಿ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by locating this Bhāṣya passage within its context: Prajāpati was said to produce a pair (mithuna), and Śaṅkara now brings that pair to conclusion with the words "yaścāsau" (that which is the Moon). The syntax (anvaya) is: "That Moon which has form, and that Prāṇa which is formless — these two together are one pair that is everything (sarvātmaka)." It was said that "these two will produce many progeny for me" — and now the question "how?" arises.

Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's answer shows how Rayi and Prāṇa, through the medium of the Saṃvatsara (Year) and related structures, become creators of progeny. That very pair (mithuna) is the Saṃvatsara — Time itself — and that Saṃvatsara is Prajāpati, because the Saṃvatsara is produced out of (nirvartyate) the pair that is of the nature of Prajāpati. Ānandagiri then unpacks the sub-point (tannirvartyatvāt): tithis (lunar days) are produced by the Moon; days and nights (ahorātras) are produced by the Sun — this is the division. Yet even though Time is produced by them, how can Time be identical to them? Ānandagiri answers by citing the principle of non-difference between cause and effect (kāryakāraṇayoḥ abhedāt) — hence "non-difference from that" (tadananyatvāt).

Ānandagiri then clarifies that it is not only through tithis etc. that the Year is produced by Moon and Sun, but also through the two ayanas (solstices) — and this is the purpose of the sub-question "tat katham?" (how so?). The real question is: from what other reason does the Year come to be produced by Moon and Sun? The correct syntactic connection (anvaya) of Śaṅkara's sentence is: the Sun travels by the Southern path while distributing worlds for those who perform only ritual action; it travels by the Northern path while distributing worlds for those who combine knowledge with action. And the word "Savitṛ" (Sun) here is an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative term) — it also implies the Moon. The Southern solstice begins with Jyeṣṭha (month), and the Northern with Mārgaśīrṣa — this is the accepted Vedic teaching. Since the two solstices are established because of the Sun (and Moon) moving along those Southern and Northern paths for the purpose of distributing worlds to the performers of action, the two ayanas are produced by them, and through the ayanas the Year too is produced by them.

To the further question "how are Moon and Sun distributors of worlds?", Ānandagiri explains: because the worlds are attained through the Southern and Northern ayanas produced by Moon and Sun, and because the worlds thus attained are themselves of the nature of Moon and Sun — therefore those two are the distributors of worlds. This is resolved by Śaṅkara's statement beginning "tad ye ha vā…" — which Ānandagiri glosses as "tat tatra."

On the definition of iṣṭa and pūrta, Ānandagiri quotes the traditional two-verse definition:

Iṣṭa is: Agnihotra, austerity (tapas), truth (satya), observance of the Vedas, hospitality (ātithya), and Vaiśvadeva rite.

Pūrta is: the digging of step-wells, wells, and tanks; construction of temples; gift of food; and planting of gardens.

On the word "kṛtam" (accomplished) — Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's "iti" after "kṛtam" draws in and covers "iṣṭāpūrte" as well as "pūrta," and the word "ādi" (etc.) stands for "datta" (what is given/donated). The meaning is: they worship and carry out only what is accomplished/conditioned — only kārya (the produced, finite). This qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) is stated as the reason for their return. Finally, Ānandagiri explains "kṛtarūpatvāt": because the lunar world itself is born from conditioned acts like iṣṭi etc., it too has the character of the kṛta (the accomplished, the finite) and is therefore impermanent — hence rebirth. The Vedic statement "imaṃ lokam" is cited as the scriptural proof (māna) for this return.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಸ — he (Prajāpati) · ಮಿಥುನಂ — the pair / dyad · ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತಿ — produces / generates · ಇತಿ — thus · ಉಪಕ್ರಾಂತಂ — what was introduced / begun earlier · ಮಿಥುನಂ — the pair · ಉಪಸಂಹರತಿ — brings to conclusion / summarises · ಯಶ್ಚಾಸಾವಿತಿ — with the words "that which is the Moon" ।

ಯಃ ಚ ಅಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ — and that which is the Moon · ಯಃ ಚ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ — and that which is the formless Prāṇa · ತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ — that one pair / dyad · ಸರ್ವಂ — all · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ — all-comprising / totality · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಏತೌ — these two · ಮೇ — for me · ಬಹುಧಾ — in many ways · ಪ್ರಜಾಃ — progeny · ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ — will produce · ಇತಿ ಉಕ್ತಂ — thus it was said · ತತ್ — that · ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಕಾರೇಣ — by what means / in what way · ಇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ — thus (Śaṅkara) raises the question · ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "how" ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ — of Rayi and Prāṇa · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the medium of the Year etc. · ಪ್ರಜಾಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಂ — the quality of being creators of progeny · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ಇತಿ — with the word "it is said" ।

ತತ್ ಏವ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಏವ — that very pair itself · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — is the Year · ಕಾಲಃ — Time ।

ಸ ಚ — and that · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — is Prajāpati · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ-ಮಿಥುನ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because it is produced from the pair that is of the nature of Prajāpati · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of being produced from it" ।

ತತ್ — this · ಉಪಪಾದಯತಿ — (Śaṅkara) establishes / proves · ಚಂದ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the word "Moon" ।

ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾಃ — produced by the Moon · ತಿಥಯಃ — the tithis (lunar days) · ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾನಿ — produced by the Sun · ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರಾಣಿ — the days-and-nights · ಇತಿ ವಿಭಾಗಃ — thus is the division / distinction ।

ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇ ಅಪಿ — even though produced by them · ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ — of Time · ಕಥಂ — how · ತದಾತ್ಮಕತಾ — identity with them / being of their nature · ಇತಿ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this doubt · ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣಯೋಃ ಅಭೇದಾತ್ — because of the non-difference of cause and effect · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of non-difference from that" ।

ನ ಕೇವಲಂ — not only · ತಿಥ್ಯಾದಿ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the medium of tithis etc. · ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by Moon etc. · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ಕಿಂ ತು — but also · ಅಯನದ್ವಯ-ದ್ವಾರಾ ಅಪಿ — through the medium of the two solstices as well · ಇತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to say this · ತಸ್ಯ ಅಯನೇ ಇತಿ ಆದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the sentence beginning "his two paths" · ತತ್-ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪೂರ್ವಕಂ — preceded by that question · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ತತ್ ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the words "how so?" ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by Moon and Sun · ಕುತಃ — from what · ಹೇತ್ವಂತರಾತ್ — from another / additional reason · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ — of those who perform only ritual action · ಲೋಕಾನ್ — worlds · ವಿದಧತ್ — while distributing · ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಯಾತಿ — travels by the Southern (path) ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ — of those who combine knowledge with action · ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ — while distributing worlds · ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಯಾತಿ — travels by the Northern · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಸವಿತಾ ಇತಿ — the word "Savitṛ (Sun)" · ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ — is an indicative term (standing for a wider class) · ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — for the Moon as well ।

ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠ-ಆದಿಃ — beginning with Jyeṣṭha (month) · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಂ — the Southern solstice · ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷ-ಆದಿಃ — beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa (month) · ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಂ — the Northern solstice · ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತಿಷು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ — as established in the Vedic texts · ತತಃ ಚ — and therefore · ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿಧಾತುಂ — in order to distribute worlds to the performers of action · ತಯೋಃ — of those two (Moon and Sun) · ದಕ್ಷಿಣ-ಉತ್ತರಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಾಭ್ಯಾಂ — by the Southern and Northern paths · ಗಮನಾತ್ — because of the movement / travel · ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ — because they are the cause of it · ಅಯನದ್ವಯ-ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ — because the two solstices are well established · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by them · ತಯೋಃ ಅಯನಯೋಃ — of those two solstices · ಇತಿ — thus · ತದ್-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through them (the solstices) · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — of the Year as well · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by them · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಯೋಃ — of Moon and Sun · ಕಥಂ — how · ಲೋಕವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಂ — the quality of being distributors of worlds · ಇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ — thus (Ānandagiri) asks · ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "how?" ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ದಕ್ಷಿಣ-ಉತ್ತರ-ಅಯನ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the Southern and Northern solstices produced by Moon and Sun · ಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇಃ — because of the attainment of worlds · ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲೋಕಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — and because the world to be attained also · ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ಆತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of Moon and Sun · ತಯೋಃ — of those two · ತದ್-ವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಂ — their quality of being distributors of those worlds · ಇತಿ — thus · ತದ್-ಯೇ ಹ ವಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ-ವಾಕ್ಯೇನ — by the sentence beginning "tad ye ha vā" · ಪರಿಹರತಿ — (Śaṅkara) resolves / answers · ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the words "tat tatra" ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಇತಿ — and with the words "iṣṭa and" ।

ಅಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ — the Agnihotra rite (daily fire offering) · ತಪಃ — austerity · ಸತ್ಯಂ — truth · ವೇದಾನಾಂ ಅನುಪಾಲನಂ — observance of the Vedas · ಆತಿಥ್ಯಂ — hospitality · ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಃ — the Vaiśvadeva rite (offering to all gods) · ಚ — and · ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಧೀಯತೇ — is called Iṣṭa ॥

ವಾಪೀ-ಕೂಪ-ತಡಾಗ-ಆದಿ — step-wells, wells, tanks, etc. · ದೇವತಾಯತನಾನಿ — temples / shrines · ಅನ್ನಪ್ರದಾನಂ — gift of food · ಆರಾಮಃ — garden / park · ಚ — and · ಪೂರ್ತಂ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಧೀಯತೇ — is called Pūrta ॥

ಇತಿ ತಯೋಃ ಭೇದಃ — thus is the distinction between the two ।

ಕೃತಂ ಇತಿ ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಇತಿ — the phrase "they worship (it as) accomplished" · ಕೃತ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಉಪರಿತನ-ಇತಿ-ಶಬ್ದಂ — the word "iti" placed after the word "kṛta" · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತಿ — the compound "iṣṭāpūrte" · ಪೂರ್ತ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಉಪರಿ — over the word "pūrta" · ಆಕೃಷ್ಯ — drawing / pulling (the iti) · ಆದಿ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಪರ್ಯಾಯತಯಾ — as a synonym for the word "ādi" (etc.) · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಇತಿ — with the word "and so on" ।

ದತ್ತಂ — what is given / donated · ಆದಿ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಅರ್ಥಃ — is the meaning of the word "ādi" ।

ಕೃತಂ ಏವ ಉಪಾಸತೇ — they worship only what is accomplished / conditioned · ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಏವ ಅನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತಿ — they carry out only what is produced / finite · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಇದಂ ಚ ವಿಶೇಷಣಂ — and this qualifier / adjective · ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ — for the return / rebirth · ಹೇತುತಯಾ — as the reason · ಉಕ್ತಂ — is stated ।

ಕೃತರೂಪ-ಇಷ್ಟ್ಯಾದಿ-ಜನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because (the Moon) is born from conditioned acts like iṣṭi etc. · ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the Moon · ಕೃತತ್ವೇನ — because of having the nature of the accomplished / conditioned · ಅನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because of impermanence · ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿಃ — there is return / rebirth · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of having the character of the accomplished" ।

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Rayi and Prāṇa (Moon/matter and Sun/life-force) are the primordial pair.
  2. The Year (Saṃvatsara) is non-different from this pair — it is produced by them through tithis, ahorātras, and the two ayanas, and cause-effect non-difference makes it identical with them.
  3. The two paths after death follow from this structure: the Southern (Pitṛyāṇa) leads to the lunar world — a finite, conditioned realm of Rayi — and return; the Northern (Devayāna) leads beyond.
  4. Iṣṭa-pūrta worshippers, treating conditioned deeds as the final end, attain only the conditioned lunar world and cycle back.
  5. Ānandagiri's contribution is to sharpen the logical spine: the identity of Time with the Rayi-Prāṇa pair rests on the Vedāntic principle of kāryakāraṇa-abheda (non-difference of effect from cause), and "Savitṛ" in the Bhāṣya functions as an upalakaṣaṇa that includes the Moon as well.
